questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I thought that the courses in Oslo looked really interesting. I was also a bit stressed at the time at looked for a place where it was easy to apply to and uncomplicated to get there. I also really liked that it was an Erasmus agreement where you could chooses courses from all faculties.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed my stay. I meet a lot of super nice people, and also because I didnt work or anything like that, I had time to 
immerse myself more in my courses and to relax and recharge.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Yes the university made everything super easy, and was easy to contact them if there was anything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There where organized a introduction week for exchange students across the social science faculty, which was a nice place to meet some people. Else most information was over email, but it was really clear. I got all the courses I wanted and everything, so I didnt have much I needed help with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I just applied through SIO as they recommended from the university. I lived at Sogn studentby which I was very happy with. It was close to campus, and I meet most of my friends there.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its very easy to get around with public transport, and you can get a decently cheap monthly transport pass as a student.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The process was pretty easy. The website is easy to navigate. The only thing is that if you want cources in norwegian you have to apply for them separately, because the exchange student website only show the english courses. It is described on the university's website how its done.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had some questions about a course in norwegian, and they responded really quickly on email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the ones I applied for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really, maybe just be sure to apply within the deadlines then you are more likely to get the courses you want.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 3 second year BA courses. I found the level of them very good. It was super interesting, but also not difficult to follow. I think the level is close to how it is at KU

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is in many ways very similar

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
SOS2603 – Nordic welfare society - contemporary perspectives
PSY2503 – Kultur- og samfunnspsykologi
SOSANT2120 – Regional Ethnography: Africa

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed both PSY2503 and SOSANT2120. Both courses was super well organized, had great lecturers and interesting readings. In SOSANT2120 we also got to work with our writing skills and worked with fictional text and movies, which was super interesting and a lot of fun. I also liked SOS2603 and learned a lot from the course, but sometimes it was a bit dry also coming from a nordic country some of what we learned I already knew a lot about.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Alcohol is very expensive and eating out as well, but I pretty much expected that. Groceries is also a bit expensive, but its similar to Copenhagen prices.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot, but I didnt use much of it. I went to the student pub a couple of times, which was fun.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed goin to smaller concerts and a music festival in Oslo. There also a lot of beautiful nature close to the city as well. Really recommend going to the islands close to the city and lakes around the city. Going to the saunas was also super nice (even though a bit expensive).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went to Lofoten for a trip with some friends in autumn. It was such a nice trip, its really beautiful so I highly recommend that.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, the culture is very similar to danish

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I really enjoyed having a course in norwegian, and here I also meet a lot of super nice norwegian students. Else through the student bar or other social activities on campus is a good place as well.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Cant really think of any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everyone is very chill and down to earth, and people are really outdoors a lot, which I really enjoyed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: thats a good question. Maybe to take it as a chance to find your own pace, and figure out what kind of themes and subject you are interested in. I really enjoyed having more time and that I was able to take the days as they come and make more spontaneous plans. Everything with the university was super easy and finding housing as well. So I would say its a super good fit also if you dont feel like spending a lot of energy on planing before.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: not really

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I really got to recharge and find time to things I love doing. I loved the nature there, and have made so many lovely 
memories with the best people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: honestly everything went pretty smooth..

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
